name: LA-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Speaker Mike Johnson holds an R+17 district with a roughly $21M-to-$269K fundraising edge
Polymarket prices Democratic chances at only about 5%
No public polls or expert ratings contest the seat's deep Republican lean
Louisiana's jungle primary splits the opposition but leaves no viable Democratic path
model.rationale: A sitting Speaker running in an R+17 district with a twenty-to-one fundraising advantage and roughly $9.6M on hand leaves the underfunded Democratic field no realistic path, and markets price Democratic victory near five percent.
model.watch: A sharp national backlash against House Republican leadership or an unexpectedly consolidated Democratic vote in a runoff scenario could narrow the margin, though not the likely outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Johnson, the Speaker of the House, seeks another term in this northwest Louisiana district, which leans Republican by about seventeen points at the presidential level. Two Democrats, Matt Gromlich and Conrad Cable, and two minor Republicans are also on the ballot under Louisiana's jungle-primary system, but none approaches Johnson's profile or resources. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a five percent chance, and no public polling challenges the district's strong Republican tilt.

Fundraising underscores the imbalance: Johnson has raised roughly twenty-one million dollars and holds more than nine million on hand, while the leading Democrat has raised about two hundred seventy thousand with little cash remaining. The national environment is competitive, but a Speaker running in a deep-red seat with this financial edge has rarely been vulnerable. The race is rated Safe Republican with high confidence.
